0.24.0.lead: From this version on, nexmail tells you after an update what has changed. This text is the first one.

sections.title: What's new, right after the update
sections.where: Banner below the top bar, later in the user menu at the top right under “What's new”
sections.body: When an update brings something new, a banner shows at the top. One click opens this text, the cross puts the banner away. It is remembered per account on the server, so on all your devices at once.

small: Large Gmail folders sync completely. Before, they stopped at 1000 messages.
Mailboxes connected through Google or Microsoft can send again.
A mailbox can be switched between a password and a consent.
If the browser refuses to register for notifications, the page now says why, and names browsers without Google's push service, such as Helium.
Very large mailboxes no longer break off the sync.

0.24.5.lead: A page the browser translated no longer takes nexmail down.

sections.title: Pages the browser translated
sections.where: Every page, when Chrome, Edge or an extension translates it
sections.body: A translated page could go blank as soon as something on it changed, because the browser had swapped the texts for its own. nexmail now keeps working on such a page.

0.25.0.lead: One-click unsubscribe, AI help for mail you receive, a command palette, and new mail now shows up by itself.

sections.title: Unsubscribe from newsletters
sections.where: Reading pane, the “Unsubscribe” button on mail from a list
sections.body: When a mail offers a way out, a button is there. If the sender is verified, nexmail does it for you, otherwise the unsubscribe page or a prepared mail opens. nexmail asks first and names the other side. The button shows on mail you open for the first time after the update.

sections.title: AI for mail you receive
sections.where: The AI page in the sidebar, switch “My received mail”, then in the reading pane and when replying
sections.body: With an AI service set up, nexmail summarises a mail, translates it, answers a question about it or drafts a reply. This is off by default because the mail goes to your service, and the operator has to allow it as well. All AI settings now live on the AI page.

sections.title: Everything from one key
sections.body: A search field finds folders, sections and the actions for the open mail, without touching the mouse.

sections.title: New mail shows up by itself
sections.where: The message list, and per mailbox the switch “See new mail right away”
sections.body: An open window now loads new mail by itself. “See new mail right away” is faster still. It keeps a second connection to the mail server open and is therefore off by default.

sections.title: Drop attachments
sections.body: Files can be dragged straight into the window. Pictures you drag into the text land at that very spot.

sections.title: Selections across mailboxes
sections.where: All inboxes and the folder column
sections.body: Delete, archive and move now work when a selection spans several mailboxes. Each mail goes to the trash or archive of its own mailbox, and undo brings them all back. Dragging into another mailbox works too.

small: Replies to invitations and out-of-office notes now go out right away. Before, they waited for the next restart.
Opening a mail no longer tears its conversation apart. Conversations that were split grow back together after the update.
Fast typing no longer loses characters, and Escape no longer throws away what you typed.
Highlighting and font size now reach the recipient.
An attachment that is still being read blocks sending instead of quietly dropping out.
Newsletters no longer show CSS in the message list.
nexmail is ready for an iPhone app, which pairs under “Connect iPhone”.

0.26.0.lead: Tasks from mail can now go to Todoist, and what you complete there, nexmail sees too.

sections.title: Connect Todoist
sections.body: Paste the API token from Todoist. nexmail checks it and keeps it encrypted. It is yours alone, everyone connects their own app. This is also where you pick the default list: your Todoist list, or nexmail's own list as before.

sections.title: List and due date when you create it
sections.body: With a connection, nexmail asks briefly: title, list and due date, with Today, Tomorrow and Next week one tap away. Only the title, the date, the sender and a link back to the mail go to Todoist, never the text of the mail. If a mail already has a task, nexmail says where instead of making a second one.

sections.title: Done in both directions
sections.body: Tick a task in nexmail and Todoist knows right away. Complete, reschedule or delete it in Todoist and nexmail follows a few minutes later, or at once when you open the task list. The date of a Todoist task is changed in Todoist.

small: Removing a Todoist task takes it out of nexmail only, it stays in Todoist.
Tasks created directly in Todoist do not show up in nexmail. The list stays the list of your mail.

0.27.0.lead: Tasks from mail can now also go to a tool of your own, through a webhook.

sections.title: Connect a webhook
sections.body: Next to Todoist there is now “Connect a webhook”. nexmail sends every task as JSON to your address, signed with a secret that is shown only once. The address is saved only after it answers a probe; “Send test” checks it again later and names the status if something is wrong.

sections.title: Send only, or report back
sections.body: With “Send only”, nexmail does not keep the task in its own list, because it gets done in the other tool. Or the tool reports back: an API key with “May tick off tasks” completes and reopens tasks through the API.

sections.title: Message text only when allowed
sections.body: A webhook can include the text of the message if its user turns it on and the operator allows it. It is off by default. Addresses on the local network work, as with calendars, only once the operator allows them.

small: For a webhook, localhost gets its own hint: inside the container it is nexmail itself, what you want is the host's address on your network.
Tick a webhook task in nexmail and the tool hears about it right away.

0.28.0.lead: A tool that gets tasks through the webhook can now also tag the message.

sections.title: Tags through the API
sections.body: An API key can now have “May tag messages”. With it, another tool adds a tag to the message of a task and removes it again, for example “Done” when the task is ticked off there. The tag goes to the mail server, just as when you set it yourself, so it also shows up in Thunderbird and on your phone. The option is separate from ticking off tasks.

sections.title: Tags in the webhook
sections.body: Every task event now lists the tags on the message, with their ID and name. The other tool knows right away how the message is tagged here.

small: If the same message sits in several folders of a mailbox, every copy gets the tag.
When a tool changes a tag through the API, nothing is sent back to the webhook.
